problem.summary: Every dotnet command fails with A compatible .NET SDK was not found when a global.json pins an SDK version that is not installed and forbids rolling forward.
problem.task_context: Running dotnet build in a repository whose global.json names an SDK newer than the one in the CI image.

solution.root_cause: global.json selects the SDK for every dotnet command run under its folder. With rollForward set to disable, only the exact version is accepted, and DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD applies to runtimes, not to SDK selection.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Install the SDK version the file names (or use an image that has it), or
change global.json: lower the version or allow rolling forward (latestFeature or latestMajor).
Run dotnet --list-sdks to see what is installed.

verification_method.description: The corrected command and verification command completed successfully in the same fixed image.

problem.summary: Installing PyYAML 5.4.1 from source fails at build time with an AttributeError about cython_sources, because its build now pulls Cython 3.
problem.task_context: Running pip install on a requirements file that pins pyyaml==5.4.1, for example in an old Docker image or CI job.

solution.root_cause: PyYAML 5.4.1 has no wheel for this Python, so pip builds it in an isolated environment that installs the newest Cython. Cython 3 broke the old setup, and a Cython installed in your own environment is not seen by that isolated build.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Install a PyYAML release that publishes wheels for your Python (6.0 or later).
If you must stay on 5.4.1, install Cython<3 and then run pip install pyyaml==5.4.1 --no-build-isolation, so that the build uses the Cython you installed.

problem.summary: pandas 2.0 removed DataFrame.iteritems and Series.iteritems, so loops written for pandas 1.x fail with an AttributeError; items() is the replacement.
problem.task_context: Upgrading a data pipeline from pandas 1.x to 2.x.

solution.root_cause: iteritems was deprecated in pandas 1.5 and removed in 2.0. items() is the same iterator under the name that Series and DataFrame share with dict.

problem.summary: SQLAlchemy 2.0 removed Engine.execute, so code that ran SQL straight on an engine fails with an AttributeError.
problem.task_context: Upgrading an application from SQLAlchemy 1.4 to 2.0.

solution.root_cause: SQLAlchemy 2.0 removed implicit execution on the engine and requires a Connection, and it no longer accepts a plain string as SQL: text() wraps it.

steps: Open a connection with engine.connect() (or engine.begin() for a transaction).
Wrap raw SQL in sqlalchemy.text().
Commit explicitly when you write: connections no longer autocommit.

problem.task_context: Running a script that was written against NumPy 1.x after pip installed NumPy 2.0.

problem.summary: JDK 23 stopped running annotation processors found on the class path unless asked, so Lombok no longer generates getters and javac reports cannot find symbol for them.
problem.task_context: Compiling a class that uses Lombok annotations after moving the build from JDK 21 to JDK 23.

solution.root_cause: From JDK 23 javac only runs annotation processors when it is told to (-proc:full, or a processor path or name). Until then it still compiled with a warning. Lombok is an annotation processor, so without it the generated members do not exist.

steps: Add -proc:full to the javac options, or list Lombok on the annotation processor path.

Use a Lombok release that supports the JDK you build with.

problem.summary: pip cannot reach a private package index whose certificate was signed by a company root CA and retries until it fails with CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED.
problem.task_context: Installing from an internal Python index inside a container that does not trust the company root.

solution.root_cause: pip uses its own CA bundle, not the system store, unless told otherwise, and the company root is in neither. Pointing --cert at the system bundle does not help for the same reason.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.

shell_commands_executed.command: pip3 install --break-system-packages --index-url https://intranet.example:8443/simple/ internal-package 2>&1 | grep -qi 'no matching distribution\|could not find a version\|no versions'
shell_commands_executed.purpose: Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Point pip at a bundle that contains the company root: pip config set global.cert /path/to/root.pem, or set PIP_CERT.
Do not use --trusted-host as a fix: it turns verification off for that host.
The index in this example returns no packages; the check only proves that the TLS handshake now succeeds.

verification_method.command: pip3 install --break-system-packages --index-url https://intranet.example:8443/simple/ internal-package 2>&1 | grep -qi 'no matching distribution\|could not find a version\|no versions'
verification_method.description: The corrected command and verification command completed successfully in the same fixed image.

problem.summary: Building a Go program that uses cgo on the golang alpine image fails because the image has no C compiler.
problem.task_context: A Dockerfile that builds with golang:alpine and a dependency that needs cgo (sqlite3, a C library binding).

solution.root_cause: The golang:alpine image is minimal and ships no gcc. cgo calls the C compiler and the C library headers, which on Alpine are gcc and musl-dev.

shell_commands_executed.command: apk add --no-cache gcc musl-dev >/dev/null && cd /w && CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./...
shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.

shell_commands_executed.command: cd /w && CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./... && echo built
shell_commands_executed.purpose: Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Install gcc and musl-dev in the build stage: apk add --no-cache gcc musl-dev.
Or avoid cgo: CGO_ENABLED=0, with a pure-Go driver or library.
Use a multi-stage build so the compiler stays out of the final image.

verification_method.command: cd /w && CGO_ENABLED=1 go build ./... && echo built
verification_method.description: The corrected command and verification command completed successfully in the same fixed image.

problem.error_message: bash: uv: command not found

failed_approaches.approach: source ~/.bashrc in the next RUN step
failed_approaches.why_it_failed: RUN uses /bin/sh, which does not read .bashrc.

problem.raw_logs:
#7 [4/6] RUN uv sync --frozen
#7 0.112 /bin/sh: 1: uv: not found
#7 ERROR: process "/bin/sh -c uv sync --frozen" did not complete successfully: exit code: 127
problem.summary: uv was installed with the official installer inside a Docker build step, but the next RUN step cannot find it because the install directory is not on PATH in non-login shells.

code_patches.description: Copy uv from its image instead of piping an installer.
code_patches.diff:
--- a/Dockerfile
+++ b/Dockerfile
@@ -3,4 +3,4 @@
 FROM python:3.13-slim
-RUN curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
+COPY --from=ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:0.8.4 /uv /uvx /bin/
 WORKDIR /app
 RUN uv sync --frozen

solution.root_cause: The installer places uv in $HOME/.local/bin and only updates shell profiles. Each Dockerfile RUN starts a fresh non-login /bin/sh that never reads them.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Install uv with the official installer.

steps: Prefer copying the uv binary from the official image instead of running the installer.
If the installer is required, add $HOME/.local/bin to PATH with ENV so every later step sees it.

verification_method.description: docker build completes and uv sync runs.

problem.summary: Gradle cannot create its cache when GRADLE_USER_HOME points at a read-only directory.
problem.task_context: Running Gradle with a cache directory mounted read-only.

solution.root_cause: Gradle needs to write metadata under GRADLE_USER_HOME; the configured cache must be writable by the build user.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Grant write access to the configured Gradle cache.
Retry Gradle and inspect its version.

problem.summary: Gradle 7 and later fail with Could not find method compile() because the compile and runtime dependency configurations were removed; build scripts written for Gradle 6 still use them.
problem.task_context: Running an old project, or an old tutorial's build.gradle, with a current Gradle.

solution.root_cause: Gradle deprecated compile and runtime in 4.x and removed them in 7.0. implementation (for dependencies the module uses) and api (for those it exposes, with the java-library plugin) replace compile; runtimeOnly replaces runtime.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Replace compile with implementation (or api for a library's public dependencies), testCompile with testImplementation, runtime with runtimeOnly.
Or run the build with the Gradle version it was written for, through its wrapper, while you migrate.

verification_method.description: The corrected command and verification command completed successfully in the same fixed image.

problem.summary: pnpm 10 does not run dependency install scripts by default, so native modules such as sqlite3 are installed without their compiled binding and fail on require.
problem.task_context: Installing a project that depends on sqlite3, bcrypt, sharp or esbuild with pnpm 10 and then running it.

solution.root_cause: Since pnpm 10 the lifecycle scripts of dependencies do not run unless the package is listed in onlyBuiltDependencies (or approved with pnpm approve-builds). A native module whose install script downloads or compiles its binding is left without it.

problem.task_context: Extracting a key or certificate from a .p12 or .pfx exported years ago, with openssl 3.x on a current Linux.

problem.summary: Node 22 requires an import attribute to load a JSON file from an ES module, so import data from './x.json' fails with ERR_IMPORT_ATTRIBUTE_MISSING.
problem.task_context: Running an ES module on Node 22 that imports a JSON file the way bundlers allow.

solution.root_cause: Node follows the import attributes proposal: a module of type JSON must be declared as JSON with `with { type: 'json' }`, so that a server cannot make an import run code by serving a different content type. The old --experimental-json-modules flag no longer changes this.

shell_commands_executed.command: cd /w && printf "import d from './x.json' with { type: 'json' };\nconsole.log(d);\n" > a.mjs
shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Add `with { type: 'json' }` to the import.
Older Node 20 releases used `assert { type: 'json' }`; use `with` on Node 22 and later.
Or read the file with fs.readFileSync and JSON.parse.

problem.summary: Every git command fails inside a CI job container because the checked-out repository is owned by a different user than the one running git.

solution.root_cause: Since git 2.35.2, git refuses to operate on repositories owned by another user (CVE-2022-24765). CI runners mount the workspace with the host user's UID while the container runs as root.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Trust only the CI workspace.
Broader alternative tried first; not recommended.

steps: Add only the workspace directory to safe.directory before any git command.
Avoid safe.directory '*', which disables the protection everywhere.

problem.error_message: anthropic.RateLimitError: Error code: 429 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'rate_limit_error'}}

failed_approaches.why_it_failed: All agents retried on the same schedule and collided again (thundering herd).

problem.raw_logs:
anthropic.RateLimitError: Error code: 429 - {'type': 'error', 'error': {'type': 'rate_limit_error', 'message': 'Number of request tokens has exceeded your per-minute rate limit'}}
retry-after: 18
problem.summary: A crew with 12 parallel agents hits 429 rate_limit_error bursts; the built-in retries all fire at the same moment and fail again.

code_patches.diff:
--- a/app/llm.py
+++ b/app/llm.py
@@ -1,6 +1,14 @@
+import asyncio, random
+_slots = asyncio.Semaphore(4)
+
 async def complete(client, **kw):
-    return await client.messages.create(**kw)
+    for attempt in range(6):
+        async with _slots:
+            try:
+                return await client.messages.create(**kw)
+            except RateLimitError as e:
+                wait = float(e.response.headers.get("retry-after", 2 ** attempt))
+        await asyncio.sleep(wait + random.uniform(0, wait))
+    raise RuntimeError("rate limited after 6 attempts")

solution.root_cause: Concurrent agents share one per-minute token budget. Synchronised retries without jitter and without honouring retry-after reproduce the burst.
steps: Cap concurrency with a shared semaphore sized to the token budget.
Honour the retry-after header and add full jitter to the backoff.

verification_method.description: The 12-agent crew completes with zero failed calls.

problem.summary: Since Java 17 the JDK's internals are encapsulated and no longer reachable by reflection, so libraries that call setAccessible on them fail with InaccessibleObjectException.
problem.task_context: Running an older library or application (Hadoop, Spark, Mockito, serialisation libraries) on Java 17.

solution.root_cause: Java 16 made strong encapsulation the default and Java 17 removed the --illegal-access escape hatch. A package of a JDK module can be used reflectively only if it is opened explicitly to the caller.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.

Upgrade the library to a release that supports Java 17 and no longer needs it.
Put the flags in JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS or the application's launcher script so that every JVM start has them.

problem.summary: go build fails with inconsistent vendoring when go.mod was changed (a version bumped or edited) but the vendor directory was not regenerated.
problem.task_context: Building a module that commits its vendor directory after a dependency version was changed in go.mod.

solution.root_cause: When a vendor directory exists the go command builds from it and checks that vendor/modules.txt matches go.mod. Editing go.mod without running go mod vendor leaves them disagreeing, and neither go mod tidy nor -mod=vendor reconciles them.

problem.summary: A Cargo.lock written by a newer Cargo (lock file version 4) cannot be read by Cargo 1.75 or older, which stops with an error naming the lock file version.
problem.task_context: Building in a container or CI image whose Rust is older than the one that last updated Cargo.lock.

solution.root_cause: Cargo 1.78 started writing lock file version 4, and Cargo versions before 1.78 do not understand it. The format is checked before anything else, so even cargo update fails.

Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Use a Rust toolchain of 1.78 or later, or
change version = 4 to version = 3 in Cargo.lock (or delete it and run cargo generate-lockfile with the older Cargo).
Pin the toolchain in rust-toolchain.toml so every machine uses the same Cargo.

problem.summary: The .NET 8 SDK cannot build a project that targets net9.0 and stops with NETSDK1045, saying the current SDK does not support targeting .NET 9.
problem.task_context: Building a project whose TargetFramework was raised to net9.0 in a CI image or container that still has the .NET 8 SDK.

solution.root_cause: An SDK can build only for target frameworks up to its own version. The SDK that builds net9.0 is .NET 9; the runtime and the targeting packs it needs are not in the 8 SDK.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Install the .NET 9 SDK, or use the mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/sdk:9.0 image for the build.
A global.json can pin the SDK version, so every machine fails or succeeds the same way.
Or lower TargetFramework to net8.0 if you do not need .NET 9.

problem.summary: curl rejects a certificate when the host in the URL is not one of the names the certificate lists, even though its CA is trusted; connecting by IP address or localhost is the usual cause.
problem.task_context: Calling an internal HTTPS service by IP address, localhost or an alias while its certificate was issued for a DNS name.

solution.root_cause: A client checks that the name in the URL matches a subject alternative name of the certificate, separately from checking the CA. The certificate lists intranet.example, so 127.0.0.1 and localhost do not match.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Use a name the certificate lists in the URL (add it to /etc/hosts or DNS if needed), or tell curl to resolve it: --resolve intranet.example:8443:127.0.0.1.
Or reissue the certificate with the other names (or IP addresses) in subjectAltName.
Do not use -k: it turns off the CA check as well.

verification_method.description: The corrected command and verification command completed successfully in the same fixed image.

problem.summary: SQLAlchemy 1.4 removed the postgres:// URL scheme, so a DATABASE_URL that starts with postgres:// (as some hosting platforms provide) fails with NoSuchModuleError.
problem.task_context: Pointing SQLAlchemy at a connection string handed out by a hosting platform.

solution.root_cause: SQLAlchemy deprecated the postgres dialect name in 1.3 and removed it in 1.4; the dialect is postgresql. The scheme must be rewritten, and a driver such as psycopg2 must be installed for the engine to load it.

ldd on the file, or readelf -l, shows the interpreter it wants.

problem.summary: Pydantic 2 refuses a @root_validator without pre=True unless it also says skip_on_failure=True; code migrated from Pydantic 1 fails at class definition.
problem.task_context: Importing a model module written for Pydantic 1 after upgrading to Pydantic 2.

solution.root_cause: Pydantic 2 deprecated @root_validator in favour of @model_validator. A post-validation root validator would otherwise run on data that already failed, so it must opt in with skip_on_failure=True; model_validator(mode='after') receives the validated model instead.

steps: Use @model_validator(mode='after') (the method takes self) or mode='before' (a classmethod taking the raw data).

problem.summary: go build fails with replacement directory does not exist when go.mod has a replace directive that points at a local path missing on this machine, as in a fresh clone or a CI job.
problem.task_context: Building a module that was developed with a replace to a sibling checkout (../lib) that is not present.

solution.root_cause: A replace directive that names a directory takes precedence over the published module, so the build needs that directory. It exists only on the machine of whoever wrote the line.

problem.summary: A go.mod that asks for a newer Go than the installed one stops the build when automatic toolchain download is switched off (GOTOOLCHAIN=local), as it is in many CI images.
problem.task_context: Building a module whose go directive was raised to 1.24 on a machine that has Go 1.22.

solution.root_cause: Since Go 1.21 the go line of go.mod is a minimum. With GOTOOLCHAIN=auto the go command downloads the toolchain it needs; with local it refuses and reports the version it requires.

Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Use a Go at least as new as the go.mod line, or let the go command download it (GOTOOLCHAIN=auto, the default).
If the module does not need the new language version, lower the go directive.
In Docker, base the image on the Go version go.mod names.

problem.task_context: Pinning an old requests next to a recent urllib3 in a requirements file.

steps: Loosen or remove the pin that conflicts (here requests), or lower the other requirement (urllib3<1.27).
Read the lines after the error: they list which package requires which range.

problem.task_context: Building a project on Rust 1.78 after cargo picked the newest releases of its dependencies.

solution.root_cause: Crates declare the oldest compiler they support (rust-version). Cargo resolves to the newest releases unless told otherwise, and a release can require a compiler newer than yours.

problem.summary: git fails to reach a server whose certificate was signed by a company root CA, with server certificate verification failed, because git does not trust that CA.
problem.task_context: Cloning or fetching over HTTPS from an internal Git server inside a container or CI image without the company CA.

solution.root_cause: The internal server's certificate chains to a root that is not in the container's trust store. Pointing git at the system bundle changes nothing, because the company root is not in it either.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Give git the company root: git config --global http.sslCAInfo /path/to/root.pem (or set GIT_SSL_CAINFO).
Better for a whole image: add the root to the system store (update-ca-certificates) so every tool trusts it.
Do not set http.sslVerify=false: it removes the protection for every repository.

verification_method.description: The corrected command and verification command completed successfully in the same fixed image.

problem.task_context: Making a static Linux binary with cargo build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.

solution.root_cause: A rustup toolchain contains the standard library only for the host target. Every other target, such as musl or wasm32, has to be installed with rustup target add.

shell_commands_executed.purpose: Apply the reproduced fix.
Verify the fix with real command output.

steps: Run rustup target add x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.

problem.summary: With module nodenext, TypeScript requires relative imports in ECMAScript modules to carry the file extension, and tsc reports TS2835 for an import written without .js.
problem.task_context: Compiling a project that moved to ES modules (type: module) and the nodenext setting.

solution.root_cause: Node's ES module loader does not guess extensions, so under nodenext TypeScript demands the path that will exist at run time: the emitted .js file, even though the source is a.ts.

problem.summary: PyTorch 2.6 changed torch.load to weights_only=True by default, so loading a checkpoint that contains arbitrary Python objects fails with an UnpicklingError.
problem.task_context: Loading a checkpoint saved with an older PyTorch, or one that stores a custom class, after upgrading to PyTorch 2.6.

solution.root_cause: Unpickling can run arbitrary code, so PyTorch 2.6 made torch.load refuse anything but tensors and a short allowlist unless you opt out. A checkpoint that pickles another class needs either that class allowlisted or weights_only=False.

steps: Only if you trust the file: pass weights_only=False.
Better: save a state_dict and load it, or allowlist the classes with torch.serialization.add_safe_globals([...]).
Never use weights_only=False on a checkpoint from an untrusted source.
